A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HBF and implicit-bias research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and matchable. v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 directional-smoothness measurements, two-parameter optimization simulations, and diagonal-network approximation-error and generalization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds numerical-integration sensitivity results and MNIST approximation-error experiments.

M1.justification: The HBF construction, correction-term recurrence, and truncation procedure are retained. Corrected third-order displays agree with formulas already present in v1's Table 1 and appendix. The newly evaluated nonlinear network does not constitute a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds MNIST classification training to the approximation-error evaluation. The CIFAR-10 experiment and synthetic two-parameter and diagonal-network regression tasks remain, making this a limited coverage extension.

E2.justification: The corresponding original experiments retain their GD, HB, RGF, and HBF comparisons. The added experiments reuse existing comparison methods; newly cited optimizer research is not introduced as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Euler integration resolutions η/100 and η/1000 alongside η/10. The new MNIST experiment uses cross-entropy, batch size 60,000, learning rate 0.01, and momentum values 0.7 and 0.8. These are added experimental settings; the original settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 and new Figure 3 test whether the two-parameter trajectory conclusions persist across three Euler integration resolutions. v1 reports only the η/10 resolution, without this solver-sensitivity check.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly states that no error bars are reported, without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Figures 3–4 report integration-resolution trajectories and MNIST error curves. The former preserve the trajectory ordering; the latter show lower settled errors for HBF than RGF at matched momentum. Original results are retained, including v1 Figures 3–4 becoming v2 Figures 5–6.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 states smoothness, bounded-derivative, and step-size/momentum validity conditions. Appendix A.2.2 replaces v1's schematic induction with explicit norm bounds tracking both accumulated error and error increments. Section 2.2.2 also corrects the third-order coefficient and restores the missing gradient-Hessian factor. These substantially revise the mathematical support for the central approximation guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: arbitrary-order HBF approximation, directional-smoothness regularization, and characterization of diagonal-network implicit bias. Additional validation does not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly discusses breakdown at large step-size/momentum combinations, conjectures a validity criterion involving η/(1−μ)^2, and distinguishes fixed-momentum asymptotics from joint parameter limits. Section 5 adds stochastic generalization as a future direction. Existing interpretations of implicit bias and generalization remain.

D1.justification: The added MNIST experiment specifies the 784–128–128–10 layer sizes, SiLU activation, batch normalization, loss, batch size, and optimization hyperparameters. Existing hardware and experimental details are retained; no new code-release or access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 expands optimizer implicit-bias positioning through Wang et al. (2021, 2022) and Zhang et al. (2024). Other additions cite stochastic continuous-time analysis and learning-rate/momentum relationships. Li et al. (2021) and Nacson et al. (2019) are removed, while the principal HBF novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 adds an intuition paragraph in Section 2, reorganizes the Appendix A proof exposition, corrects theorem cross-references, and adds acknowledgments and a checklist. Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Document-wide NeurIPS retypesetting changes fonts, margins, text density, title layout, and display sizes. v2 also adds a proof-flow diagram and two experimental figures, while resizing and relocating retained figures and tables. This is a substantial visual-layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the paper's central guarantee: it replaces the terse error induction with explicit bounds, states previously implicit validity restrictions, and repairs inconsistent third-order equations. The Euler-resolution check and nonlinear MNIST experiment also address important gaps in validation. Although the proposed composite-parameter validity criterion remains conjectural, the combined improvements materially strengthen theoretical accountability and empirical support without changing the core method.
